question.problem:
A continuous random variable $X$ has the probability density function 

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}, & -1<x<0, \\ \frac{4}{3}\,x, & 0\le x<1.\end{aligned}
$$

Calculate $\text{E}[{X}^{2}].$
question.worked_solution:
For a continuous random variable $X$ with probability density function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S,$ the expected value of ${X}^{2}$ is given by

$$
\text{E}[{X}^{2}]={\int }_{S}{x}^{2}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

So, we compute the expected value of ${X}^{2}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}{x}^{2}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}{x}^{2}\cdot {x}^{2}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{2}\cdot \frac{4}{3}\,x\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}{x}^{4}\,\text{d}x+\frac{4}{3}{\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{3}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{5}\,{x}^{5}\,{|}_{-1}^{0}+\frac{1}{3}\,{x}^{4}\,{|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}(0+1)+\frac{1}{3}(1-0) \\  & =\frac{1}{5}+\frac{1}{3} \\  & =\frac{8}{15}.\end{aligned}
$$
